question: Does compliant documentation change top3 discovery of equal finite-domain behavior compared with code tokens?
domain: All integer inputs 0..255, scalar u16 output; no effects, no performance equivalence
representation: Lowercased Unicode word tokens of length >=2; raw count times smoothed IDF; L2 norm; cosine. Code uses body only. Doc uses field values only.
fit: Code fit on all eight bodies; docs fit on all eight complete documents. Same vocabulary and IDF retained for every intervention.
fusion: 0.5*code_cosine + 0.5*doc_cosine; untuned diagnostic reference, not a calibrated new method
ranking: Positive scores rounded to 12 decimals descending, sorted ID pair ascending for ties; unordered unique pairs
truth: Equality of complete 256-value output vectors after each implementation passes its formula oracle. Labels never used by ranker. Not refactoring desirability.
stop: Rust runs twice identically, all formula checks pass, all 24 condition-repeat outputs archived, input hashes verified; retain negative results without tuning
limits: Synthetic small development corpus designed by same researcher; code/doc formulations can bias retrieval; not independent holdout, whole-repo accuracy, architecture or optimization evidence
